result.title: TSBPO: Tree-Structured Branching for Policy Optimization in Interactive Language Agents
result.summary: Training interactive language agents from terminal outcomes poses three coupled problems: which task and state continuations to sample, how to assign delayed feedback to decisions, and how to aggregate token losses for multi-token actions. We present TSBPO, a tree-structured sampling-to-update paradigm that addresses these problems within one training loop. A likelihood-fitted Root/Branch allocator uses retained task and state evidence to target continuations likely to produce contrasting terminal outcomes under fixed rollout budgets. On the resulting replayed physical trees, trajectory advantages compare immediate sibling segments, while observation-group step advantages compare outcomes at matched task/observation states. The actor then sums clipped token surrogates over each complete response and normalizes across active turns, avoiding response-length averaging in the policy-gradient term. With a Qwen2.5-1.5B actor, fixed checkpoints obtain 97.79% seen and 96.64% unseen stochastic success on ALFWorld and an 81.07% per-episode success rate over six stochastic episodes for each of the 500 WebShop test goals. A WebShop step-term ablation yields 75.93% at the same update-100 evaluation; an ALFWorld aggregation comparison shows higher observed command validity with complete-turn weighting. These results support the evaluated training configuration on two interactive benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TSBPO 训练范式，用 Root/Branch 分配器在固定 rollout 预算下采样更易产生对比性终局的任务与状态续接，并在回放树上以兄弟段比较和同状态分组比较做延迟反馈的优势分配，同时按完整回答求和、跨轮归一化 token 损失；在 ALFWorld 与 WebShop 上报告成功率的消融对比。
AI.relevance_reason: 纯文本交互智能体，无视觉与 latent 状态，但其「在匹配状态下对比结果以分配延迟反馈」和分支采样式贡献分配，可供核查 LVR 中多步 latent 推理的信用分配与 rollout 预算投向对比性证据的问题。
